title: Use Consensus in ChatGPT, Claude, Copilot, or with the API
snippet:
If you already use ChatGPT, Claude, or Microsoft 365 Copilot, connect Consensus to it. Your assistant can then search over 400 million scholarly articles, including 350 million peer-reviewed research papers, apply academic filters, hand research questions to the Consensus research agent, and cite real research instead of answering from memory.

### Connect another tool
Using a different assistant or tool, such as Cursor, VS Code, or Claude Code? Connect it to the Consensus MCP server directly. MCP (Model Context Protocol) is a standard way for AI assistants to use outside tools. The server is hosted, so there’s nothing to install:
```
https://mcp.consensus.app/mcp
```
## Set up your client
Step-by-step connection guides for Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code, Windsurf, Gemini Spark, Copilot Studio, and any other MCP client.
## What your assistant can do
**Search.** The `search` tool returns ranked papers with title, authors, journal, publication year, citation count, study type, a key takeaway, and a link to the paper on Consensus. On paid plans it also returns query-relevant excerpts from open-access papers, so your assistant can quote the passage behind each claim. Your assistant can pass the same filters Research Agent uses:
- Year range, study type, and journal quartile (SJR)
- Human and controlled studies, minimum sample size, minimum citations
- Medical mode, open access only, exclude preprints
- Study duration and country

## Supported clients
Claude (web, desktop, and Claude Code), ChatGPT and ChatGPT Deep Research, Codex, Cursor, VS Code and GitHub Copilot, Windsurf, Gemini Spark, Microsoft 365 Copilot and Copilot Studio, and any client that supports remote MCP servers.
- Claude
- ChatGPT
- Microsoft 365 Copilot
Open **Settings › Connectors**, search for Consensus, and click **+**. Then switch it on from the **+** menu in any chat under **Connectors**.

3. Ask a research question, and Copilot calls Consensus to find relevant papers.

title: GitHub - Consensus-NLP/consensus-mcp: Official Consensus MCP server. Semantic search over 400M+ research papers, including all of PubMed, for Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor and any MCP client.
snippet:
# Consensus MCP Server: Scientific Literature Search for Claude, ChatGPT and Cursor

The official Consensus MCP server gives Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, VS Code, Microsoft 365 Copilot, Perplexity and any other MCP client semantic search over **400M+ scholarly articles, including 350M peer-reviewed papers and all of PubMed**. Your assistant can find research papers, filter them by study design and journal quality, and give answers that cite real studies, without leaving the chat.
It's a hosted remote server, so there's nothing to install. Connect, ask a research question, and get back ranked papers with DOIs, citation counts, study type, sample size and a one-line takeaway.
**Server URL**
```
https://mcp.consensus.app/mcp
```
## Why use the Consensus MCP server
- **One index for all of science.** Biomedical, clinical, psychology, computer science, economics, materials and every other field. The index includes all of PubMed and is updated weekly.
- **Semantic search, not keyword matching.** Results are ranked by how well they answer the question, so "does creatine help memory in older adults" works as written. No Boolean strings or MeSH terms needed.
- **Evidence-quality filters.** Limit results to RCTs, meta-analyses or systematic reviews (19 study types), human or controlled studies, a minimum sample size, top-quartile journals (SJR), recent years, clinical guidelines, or Medical mode (about 8M papers from the top 1,000 medical journals).

No account is needed to try it. Sign in for more papers per search and richer results (plans).
### Claude (web and desktop)
One click: open [Consensus in the Claude directory](https://claude.ai/directory/65247229-f0c7-49df-9044-fcbb8b3894c6) and click **Connect**. Or manually:
1. Open [claude.ai](https://claude.ai) (or the Claude desktop app) and go to **Settings**
2. Select **Connectors**, then **Browse connectors**
3. Search for **Consensus** and click **Connect**
4. Approve the sign-in with your Consensus account (or continue without one at reduced limits)
5. Ask a research question in any chat; Consensus appears in the tools menu

### Everything else
Any client that supports remote MCP servers (Streamable HTTP) works. Point it at `https://mcp.consensus.app/mcp` and sign in with OAuth, or send an API key as a Bearer token:
```
Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY
```

title: Getting Started with the Consensus MCP
snippet:
The Consensus MCP server enables AI assistants like ChatGPT, Claude, and other MCP-compatible clients to search over 200 million peer-reviewed academic research papers directly from the conversation.
##
Getting Started
Consensus MCP lets AI assistants search 200+ million peer-reviewed research papers. Connect your preferred client below — you'll be searching in under 2 minutes.
> **Server URL:**`https://mcp.consensus.app/mcp`
>
> The `/mcp` path is required. Using `https://mcp.consensus.app` alone will not work.
---
##
Connect Your Client
###
Claude Desktop
1. Go to **Settings → Connectors**
2. Click **Browse Connectors**
3. Search for **Consensus**
4. Click **Connect** — OAuth sign-in will open automatically
###
ChatGPT
1. Click **Apps** from the left sidebar
2. Search for **Consensus**
3. Click **Connect** and sign in with your Consensus account
Search results display in an interactive widget showing top papers with citations and direct links.
Consensus also works with **ChatGPT Deep Research**. When Deep Research uses the Consensus app, it can search Consensus for relevant papers and fetch full paper details for cited results.

Claude Code
```
claude mcp add --transport http consensus https://mcp.consensus.app/mcp
```
OAuth will open in your browser automatically on first use. You can also trigger it manually with the `/mcp` command inside Claude Code.
###
Codex
```
codex mcp add consensus --url https://mcp.consensus.app/mcp codex mcp login consensus
```
###
Cursor
Add via **Settings → Tools & MCP → New MCP Server**, or edit your config directly:
```
{ "mcpServers": { "Consensus": { "command": "npx", "args": [ "-y", "mcp-remote@latest", "https://mcp.consensus.app/mcp" ] } } }
```
###
VS Code (GitHub Copilot)
Add to your MCP configuration:
```
{ "servers": { "Consensus": { "url": "https://mcp.consensus.app/mcp" } }, "inputs": [] }
```
In the text box click the '+' button -> Tools... -> Select the `search` tool call from the Consensus MCP.
###
Windsurf
Add via **Settings → Cascade → MCP Servers**, or edit your config directly:
```
{ "mcpServers": { "consensus": { "serverUrl": "https://mcp.consensus.app/mcp" } } }
```
###
Other MCP Clients
Any MCP compatible client can connect using the server URL `https://mcp.consensus.app/mcp` with HTTP transport. If your client supports OAuth, authentication will be handled automatically.

title: Connection reference
snippet:
## Endpoint and transport
| | |
|---|---|
| **MCP endpoint** | `https://mcp.consensus.app/mcp` |
| **Transport** | Streamable HTTP |
| **Responses** | Buffered JSON. There is no SSE endpoint and the server never returns SSE event streams. |
| **Sessions** | Stateless. No `Mcp-Session-Id`, no session affinity, so your gateway needs no sticky-session configuration. |
| **Tools** | `search`, plus the thread tools `create_thread`, `get_thread`, `add_to_thread`, and `find_threads` for signed-in accounts and API keys, and `get_full_text` for paid plans. See the [tool reference](/mcp-tools/quickstart). |
All MCP and JSON-RPC calls must target the `/mcp` path. The bare host `https://mcp.consensus.app/` only answers health checks and OAuth discovery.
Where a product lets you choose a transport, pick **Streamable HTTP** explicitly. Some gateways default to SSE, which will fail against this server.
## Authentication
Two options. For a shared, server-side gateway credential, use an API key.
- API key (recommended for gateways)
- OAuth 2.0 (per-user)
A single opaque credential sent as a bearer token:
```
Authorization: Bearer ak_live_...
```
It lives entirely server-side, involves no user redirect and no token refresh, and maps to your Enterprise tier. Generate one from your Consensus account: profile icon → **API & MCP Dashboard** → **Keys and clients** → **New key**. The full key is shown once.Treat it like a password: keep it out of client-side code, public repositories, and screenshots.
Authorization-code flow only. There is no client-credentials grant, so OAuth always involves a per-user consent step; each user signs in to their own Consensus account.
| | |
|---|---|
| **Authorization URL** | `https://consensus.app/oauth/authorize/` |
| **Token URL** | `https://consensus.app/oauth/token/` |
| **Dynamic Client Registration** | `https://consensus.app/oauth/register/` (RFC 7591) |
| **Scope** | `search`. Request `scope=search` or omit it; it’s the default. This is not an OIDC provider, so there are no `openid` or `email` scopes. |
| **PKCE** | Required. `S256` only; requests without a `code_challenge` are rejected. |

Gateways that support automatic configuration can read these:
- `https://mcp.consensus.app/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource` — points to the authorization server
- `https://consensus.app/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` — full metadata: endpoints, scopes, and `S256`

title: LiteLLM MCP Gateway
snippet:
LiteLLM’s MCP Gateway exposes upstream MCP servers on its `/mcp` endpoint and scopes them by key and team. Register Consensus in the UI under **MCP Servers › Add New MCP Server**, or in `config.yaml`.
LiteLLM’s `transport` defaults to `"sse"`. Set it to `"http"` or the connection will fail; Consensus has no SSE endpoint.
## Shared API key
```
mcp_servers:
consensus:
url: "https://mcp.consensus.app/mcp"
transport: "http"
auth_type: "bearer_token"
auth_value: os.environ/CONSENSUS_API_KEY
description: "Search 400M+ scholarly articles, including 350M peer-reviewed papers"
```
`bearer_token` sends the value as `Authorization: Bearer <auth_value>`. If you’d rather set the header explicitly:
```
mcp_servers:
consensus:
url: "https://mcp.consensus.app/mcp"
transport: "http"
static_headers:
Authorization: "Bearer ak_live_..."
```
## Per-user OAuth
Consensus supports Dynamic Client Registration, so point LiteLLM at the registration endpoint and it registers itself:
```
mcp_servers:
consensus:
url: "https://mcp.consensus.app/mcp"
transport: "http"
auth_type: oauth2
oauth2_flow: authorization_code
authorization_url: "https://consensus.app/oauth/authorize/"
token_url: "https://consensus.app/oauth/token/"
registration_url: "https://consensus.app/oauth/register/"
scopes: ["search"]
```
LiteLLM’s callback is `https://<PROXY_BASE_URL>/ui/mcp/oauth/callback`; set `PROXY_BASE_URL` when running behind an ingress. `oauth2_flow` is required on every `oauth2` entry. If your clients already hold a Consensus-issued token, `auth_type: true_passthrough` forwards it unchanged.
## Notes
- Changing `server_id` after keys and teams have been granted access breaks those permissions.
- On aggregate endpoints, per-server credentials go in `x-mcp-consensus-authorization`.

title: Setting Up the Consensus AI Connect (Consensus MCP Server)
snippet:
AI Agent Connect, powered by The Consensus MCP (Model Context Protocol) Server, enables you to access your Consensus demos directly within an MCP-compatible app. This guide will walk you through the complete setup process.
---
#### **Prerequisites**
Before you begin, you will need:
- An AI Agent compatible with MCP Servers
- Consensus Admin access
- Admin access to compatible MCP Clients
- The Consensus MCP Server URL: [https://mcp.goconsensus.com/mcp](https://mcp.goconsensus.com/mcp)
Find security information on the Consensus MCP server:
- [Consensus AI Connect - MCP Server Security Information](https://support.goconsensus.com/mcp-server-security-information)
---
#### **Setting Up MCP Server for Claude Desktop**
*For additional information, visit the Claude Support page found here:*[*https://support.claude.com/en/articles/11175166-getting-started-with-custom-connectors-using-remote-mcp*](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/11175166-getting-started-with-custom-connectors-using-remote-mcp)
**Admin Setup Steps:**
1. **Navigate to Admin Settings**
- Go to[ Admin settings > Connectors](https://claude.ai/admin-settings/connectors)
2. **Add Custom Connector**
- Click "Add custom connector" at the bottom of the Connectors section
- Enter your Consensus MCP server URL
3. **Save Configuration**
- Click "Add" to finish configuring the connector
- The connector will now appear in your organization's available connectors list with a "Custom" label
**Important Notes for Admins:**
- Only Owners can add custom connectors to Team/Enterprise organizations
- Once added, individual users must authenticate with their own credentials
- Each user will only be able to access Consensus data they have permission to see
- You can monitor and manage the connector through Admin settings

**User Setup Steps:**
1. **Navigate to Settings**
- Go to[ Settings > Connectors](https://claude.ai/settings/connectors)
2. **Find the Consensus Connector**
- Look for "Consensus" in the Connectors list
- It will have a "Custom" label indicating it was added by your admin
3. **Connect and Authenticate**
- Click "Connect" next to the Consensus connector
- You'll be redirected to complete the OAuth authentication flow
- Sign in with your Consensus credentials
- Review and approve the requested permissions
- You'll be redirected back to Claude once authentication is complete
4. **Enable in Conversations**
- In any chat, click the "+" button in the lower left
- Select "Connectors"
